title: Early Surgical Treatment of Children with Deep Burns of the Feet
content: Introduction: Children are particularly vulnerable to foot burns due to slower reactions to danger, which increase the likelihood of deep burns. Early surgical intervention is frequently hindered by significant blood loss during excision. Material and methods: This retrospective study analyzed outcomes for 59 pediatric patients treated for deep burns between 2015 and 2022 at Samarkand Centre of Emergency Medical Care, Uzbekistan. Patients were divided into two groups based on the timing of surgical intervention. Group 1 (21 patients) received early excision and skin grafting under a tourniquet within 3–4 days of injury. Group 2 (38 patients) underwent traditional treatment, including delayed excision and grafting. Results: Early intervention reduced blood loss, shortened operative time, minimized postoperative complications, and improved cosmetic outcomes. Hospital stays averaged 10 days for Group 1, compared to 25 days for Group 2. Early surgical treatment under a tourniquet is effective in enhancing recovery and reducing complications with deep foot burns. Conclusions: The procedures helped to improve the general condition of patients, shortened their stay in hospital and also reduced expenses and lessened joint deformities.
